::: {#rem-cross-product-matrix}
#### Cross-product matrix as a matrix product

Let $\design$ be the matrix whose rows are the transposed [term vectors](#def-term-vector) $\tp{\termvec{i}}$, $i \in I$.
The cross-product matrix then equals the matrix product

$$
A = \tp{\design} \design.
$$

Its diagonal entries are sums of squares of one term over the training set.
Its off-diagonal entries are sums of cross-products of two different terms.
Statisticians therefore call $A$ the sum-of-squares and cross-products (SSCP) matrix of the terms.
When every column of $\design$ has mean zero, $A / (\abs{I} - 1)$ is the sample covariance matrix of the terms.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
